title: Low‐dose aspirin does not lower in vivo platelet activation in healthy smokers

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Smoking causes atherosclerosis, and smokers have increased thromboxane (TXA<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>) formation. As aspirin inhibits TXA<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> production we speculated that smokers would preferentially profit from inhibition of the TXA<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> pathway by aspirin. Increased expression of P‐selectin, a constituent of the alpha‐granules of platelets, and increased levels of circulating (c)P‐selectin in plasma are markers for platelet activation.</jats:p><jats:p>The aim of this study was to compare P‐selectin expression on platelets between smokers and nonsmokers, and to compare with placebo the effect of 2 weeks administration of 100 mg/d aspirin on platelet activation in smokers. Smokers exhibited higher P‐selectin expression on platelets than non‐smokers (2.7 ± 1.8% <jats:italic>v</jats:italic> 1.6 ± 0.6%, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = 0.018), thus confirming increased platelet activation. Aspirin did not reduce platelet activation as demonstrated by unchanged P‐selectin expression on platelets and cP‐selectin plasma levels.</jats:p>
